{{nihongo|'''Okunitama Shrine'''|大国玉神社 (桜川市)}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Hitachi Province]].

Its nickname is Myōjin-sama<ref name="annai">Ibaraki Prefectural Shrine Association: [http://www.ibaraki-jinjacho.jp/ibaraki/kensei/jinja/12178.html Shrine guide within the prefecture]. Retrieved November 16, 2013.</ref>. Its former name was Kashima Daimyōjin (Kashima Myōjin)<ref>''Shinpen Hitachi no Kuni-shi''.</ref>. It is listed as a {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Shikinaisha}} ({{ill|Hitachi Province|cs|Provincie Hitači|de|Provinz Hitachi|es|Provincia de Hitachi|fa|ولایت هیتاچی|fr|Province de Hitachi|gl|Provincia de Hitachi|hak|Hitachi-koet|id|Provinsi Hitachi|it|Hitachi (provincia)|ja|常陸国|ko|히타치국|lt|Hitačio žemė|nl|Hitachi (provincie)|pt|Província de Hitachi|ru|Хитати (провинция)|simple|Hitachi Province|sk|Hitači (provincia)|sr|Провинција Хитачи|tr|Hitachi (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Хітаті|zh|常陸國|zh_min_nan|Hitati-kok|zh_yue|常陸國|qid=Q1055353}}, Makabe District, minor shrine). Its former rank was {{ill|Q712534|lt=Gōsha}}. It is also written in old characters as '''大國玉神社'''.

=== History ===
The founding date is unknown. Shrine tradition says it was founded in the {{ill|Yōrō|de|Yōrō (Ära)|es|Yōrō|fa|یورو (دوره)|fr|Ère Yōrō|ia|Yoro|id|Yōrō|it|Yōrō (era)|ja|養老|ko|요로 (연호)|ru|Ёро (нэнго)|simple|Yōrō|sr|Јоро|tr|Yōrō|uk|Йоро (ненґо)|zh|養老 (日本)|zh_yue|養老|qid=Q1373061}} era ({{ill|717|ab|717|af|717|am|717 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|717|ar|717|ary|717|ast|717|az|717|azb|۷۱۷ (میلادی)|be|717|be_x_old|717|bg|717|bn|৭১৭|bpy|মারি ৭১৭|br|717|bs|717.|ca|717|cdo|717 nièng|ceb|717|ckb|٧١٧|crh|717|cs|717|cv|717|cy|717|da|717|de|717|el|717|eml|717|eo|717|es|717|et|717|eu|717|fa|۷۱۷ (میلادی)|fi|717|fo|717|fr|717|fy|717|ga|717|gan|717年|gd|717|gl|717|hak|717-ngièn|he|717|hi|717|hr|717.|ht|717 (almanak jilyen)|hu|717|hy|717|id|717|ilo|717|io|717|is|717|it|717|ja|717年|jv|717|ka|717|kaa|717|kk|717 жыл|ko|717년|la|717|lb|717|lij|717|lmo|717|lt|717 m.|lv|717. gads|map_bms|717|mdf|717|mg|717|mhr|717|mk|717|mr|इ.स. ७१७|mrj|717 и|ms|717|mzn|۷۱۷|nah|717|nap|717|nds|717|new|सन् ७१७|nl|717|nn|717|no|717|nrm|717|nso|717|oc|717|or|୭୧୭|os|717-æм аз|pl|717|pnb|717|pt|717|qu|717|ro|717|ru|717 год|rue|717|sa|७१७|scn|717|sd|717ع|sh|717.|shn|717|si|717|sk|717|sl|717|smn|717|sq|717|sr|717|su|717|sv|717|sw|717|tg|Соли 717|th|พ.ศ. 1260|tk|717|tl|717|tly|717|tr|717|tt|717 ел|uk|717|ur|717ء|uz|717|vec|717|vi|717|vls|717|war|717|wuu|717年|xmf|717|zh|717年|zh_min_nan|717 nî|zh_yue|717年|qid=Q23532|lt=717}}–{{ill|724|Q23549|qid=Q23549}})<ref name="annai"/>. Another tradition places it in the {{ill|Tenchō|Q1373138|qid=Q1373138}} era ({{ill|824|Q30353|qid=Q30353|lt=824}}–{{ill|834|Q30381|qid=Q30381}}).

It is an ancient shrine recorded in the {{ill|Rikkokushi|Q1151168|qid=Q1151168}} and the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}.
* {{ill|Shoku Nihon Kōki|Q1041301|qid=Q1041301}}
** Vol. 6: In the reign of {{ill|Emperor Ninmyō|Q349271|qid=Q349271}}, 3rd month of {{ill|Jōwa (Heian period)|de|Jōwa|es|Jōwa (período Heian)|fa|جووا (دوره هی‌آن)|fr|Ère Jōwa (Heian)|ia|Jowa|id|Jōwa|ja|承和 (日本)|ko|조와 (834년)|ru|Дзёва (Хэйан)|simple|Jōwa (Heian period)|sr|Џова (Хејан период)|tr|Jōwa (Heian)|uk|Дзьова (ненґо)|zh|承和 (日本)|zh_yue|承和|qid=Q1075605|lt=Jōwa}} 4 ({{ill|837|Q25093|qid=Q25093}}), together with Sashino no Kami of Niihari District, it appears as "'''Ōkunitama no Kami of Makabe District'''" with the note "並預官社。以比年特有靈驗也" (it was admitted to the government shrine register due to especially notable divine efficacy in that year).
** Vol. 15: In the same era, year 12 ({{ill|846|Q30454|qid=Q30454}}), "奉授常陸國无位'''大國玉神'''從五位下" (granted Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade).
* {{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Q1052981|qid=Q1052981}}
** Vol. 5: In the reign of {{ill|Emperor Seiwa|Q349243|qid=Q349243}}, 9th month of {{ill|Jōgan|Q1075635|qid=Q1075635|lt=Jōgan}} 3 ({{ill|861|Q23913|qid=Q23913}}), "授常陸國從五位下'''主玉神'''從五位上" (promoted to Junior Fifth Rank, Upper Grade).
** Among historical records, only the ''Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku'' records the deity name as "Shutama no Kami"; whether this is the same deity as Ōkunitama no Kami is unclear. Since there are three shrines in Ibaraki claiming to correspond to "Shutama no Kami" (Oishi Shrine in Hokota City, and Kamo-Ōkami-Miko-Shutama Shrine in Sakuragawa City), this is treated as a {{ill|Shikinai Ronsha|Q135022904|qid=Q135022904}} (disputed corresponding shrine).
* {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}
** In {{ill|Engi (era)|Q1374325|qid=Q1374325}} 5 (927), listed as one minor shrine in Makabe District, Hitachi Province: "'''Ōkunitama Shrine'''" (one of {{ill|Hitachi Province|cs|Provincie Hitači|de|Provinz Hitachi|es|Provincia de Hitachi|fa|ولایت هیتاچی|fr|Province de Hitachi|gl|Provincia de Hitachi|hak|Hitachi-koet|id|Provinsi Hitachi|it|Hitachi (provincia)|ja|常陸国|ko|히타치국|lt|Hitačio žemė|nl|Hitachi (provincie)|pt|Província de Hitachi|ru|Хитати (провинция)|simple|Hitachi Province|sk|Hitači (provincia)|sr|Провинција Хитачи|tr|Hitachi (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Хітаті|zh|常陸國|zh_min_nan|Hitati-kok|zh_yue|常陸國|qid=Q1055353}}'s 28 shrines).

In the 11th month of {{ill|Genroku|Q1325001|qid=Q1325001}} 12 ({{ill|1699|Q7710|qid=Q7710}}), {{ill|Tokugawa Mitsukuni|Q1194944|qid=Q1194944}} dedicated banners of the four gods and halberd-banners of the sun and moon<ref name="annai"/>.

In the 4th month of {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} 5 ({{ill|1872|Q7753|qid=Q7753}}), it was ranked as a gōsha.

In October {{ill|Heisei era|Q234510|qid=Q234510}} 4 ({{ill|1992|Q2060|qid=Q2060}}), shrine buildings were renovated.

Old regional gazetteers introduce a scenic site called the "Seven Wells of Okunitama": Miyamae no I, Kugutsu I, Kōshinmae I, Kisaki no I, Fukusen Koshiki I, Fukusen Kome I, and Fukusen Sake I.

=== Enshrined deities ===
; Main deity
: {{ill|Ōkuninushi|abstract|Q276944|ca|Ōkuninushi|es|Ōkuninushi|fa|اوکونینوشی|fr|Ōkuninushi|hu|Ókuninusi|id|Ookuninushi|it|Ōkuninushi|ja|大国主|ko|오오쿠니누시|mni|ꯑꯣꯀꯨꯅꯤꯅꯨꯁꯤ|pl|Ōkuninushi|pt|Ookuninushi|ru|Окунинуси|simple|Ōkuninushi|sr|Okuninuši|sv|Ōkuninushi|tr|Ōkuninushi|uk|Окунінуші|vi|Ōkuninushi|zh|大國主|qid=Q276944|lt=Ōkuninushi-no-Mikoto}}
; Associated deities
: {{ill|Takemikazuchi|lt=Takemikazuchi|Q1502690|qid=Q1502690|qid=Q1502690|lt=Takemikazuchi-no-Mikoto}}, {{ill|Kamo-wake-ikazuchi-no-Kami|Q11634943|qid=Q11634943|lt=Wakeikazuchi-no-Mikoto}}

''Shinpen Hitachi no Kuni-shi'' states: "Called Kashima Daimyōjin. According to shrine tradition, there were two enshrined deities: the east was called Nantai-gū, and the west Nyotai-gū, also called Monoimi-gū." In earlier times it was called Kashima Daimyōjin, and there was a paired two-shrine structure of a male-deity shrine and female-deity shrine. The integration of Nyotai-gū is described as "at the beginning of Meiji, the priestly office of the western shrine was dissolved and succeeded by the priest of the eastern shrine"<ref>Hitachi no Kuni-kei Sugiyama Shiki.</ref>, indicating that this occurred in the Meiji period. The present shrine site is considered the continuation of Nantai-gū.

The old site of Nyotai-gū is unknown, but Kisaki Shrine in the precincts enshrines Ōkuninushi's principal consort {{ill|Suseri-Hime|Q8191715|qid=Q8191715|lt=Suseribime-no-Mikoto}}. There is also another Kisaki Shrine east of Ōkunitama Shrine (an independent shrine: {{ill|Non-denominational|Q7882536|qid=Q7882536|lt=independent shrine}}), but its deity is "Kimi no Gozen," wife of {{ill|Taira no Masakado|Q1207652|qid=Q1207652}}, and its {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=shintai}} is a wooden female figure (Kisaki Shrine sacred image; designated cultural property of Sakuragawa City).

Regarding the deity, one account says: "Perhaps Kashima Ōkami was enshrined; this is also evidenced by 23 songs transmitted at this shrine, all praising the divine power of Kashima deity." It further argues that "Ōkunitama-no-Kami" or "Kuni-gami" was an honorific title for deities who pacified each province, and in Hitachi Province it was another name for Takemikazuchi-no-Mikoto.

=== Festivals ===
* {{ill|January 3|Q2156|qid=Q2156}}: Kuwe no Matsuri (Kuwauchi Festival) – a {{ill|Ta-asobi|Q11577415|qid=Q11577415}} ritual praying for a good harvest; designated intangible folk cultural property of Sakuragawa City.
* {{ill|January 4|Q2168|qid=Q2168}}: Sayado Meguri Festival – formally called "Ōkunitama Shrine Mass Procession of the Seventy-Five Subsidiary Shrines"; participants carry a large sacred sakaki branch and beat drums while touring subsidiary shrines in the Okunitama district to pray for household safety; designated intangible folk cultural property of Sakuragawa City.
